summary: Educational seminars, conferences, and professional/association information services; low capital requirements and abundant online substitutes keep profits thin for new entrants.
Biomedical, pharmaceutical and scientific research and laboratory-testing services; specialized know-how and patents protect discoveries, favoring the firms that get there first.
Specialty and online retail store services plus consumer-goods marketing/promotion; intense competition from big-box and e-commerce incumbents erodes new-entrant margins.
A heterogeneous mix of religious/charitable programming, consumer education and mobile apps; low capital needs and easy imitation leave little durable advantage.
Floor coverings, mats and commercial printing products; retail and distribution buyer power keeps this a moderate-barrier, low-margin manufacturing category.
Electronic sensing, control and instrumentation apparatus for industrial and vehicle applications; manufacturing scale and certification requirements favor incumbents.
Metal and wood building hardware, fasteners and construction materials; contractor and distributor buyer power limits pricing for commodity-like products.
Pet food, treats, accessories and pet-care services; a growing category crowded with established brands and dominated by big pet retailers.
Consumer electronics accessories, cables and peripherals; commodity products sourced from contract manufacturers are trivially copied, making this an unattractive segment.
Apparel, bags and footwear; fashion goods are easy to design and produce but brand equity and retail distribution held by incumbents capture most value.

Online marketplaces, business directories and digital advertising/marketing services; network effects reward early movers like established directories, but low technical barriers invite constant entry.
Books, printed educational materials and paper/stationery goods; digital substitution and retailer power keep this a structurally low-margin publishing category.
Decorative giftware, figurines and household glass/metal goods; low differentiation and easy imitation leave little lasting advantage for entrants.
Conferences, trade shows, educational seminars and association/ministry services; minimal capital requirements and high substitutability limit long-run profits.
Fragrances, candles and scented personal-care products; formulations are easily copied via contract manufacturing, so brand and distribution decide outcomes.
Automotive lubricants, fuels and vehicle repair/maintenance services; a mature aftermarket with established distribution and service networks.
Respiratory and other therapeutic pharmaceuticals plus related medical devices (inhalers, hearing aids); regulatory approval and patents give first movers durable protection.
Trade-show, exhibition, lobbying and promotional/advertising services for businesses; low capital requirements keep this fragmented and competitive.
Household furniture, lighting fixtures and storage goods; easily copied designs and dominant big-box/online retail buyers limit entrant profits.
Specialty construction chemicals, coatings, sealants and soil treatments; technical formulation know-how gives moderate protection to innovators.
Community, legal, eldercare, childcare and wellness-education services; licensure adds a modest barrier, but the field stays fragmented and low-margin.
Paints, coatings, cleaning preparations and vehicle-cleaning services; established brands and retail distribution dominate this chemically commoditized category.
Medical disposables and consumables (bandages, syringes, gloves, dental apparatus); hospital group-purchasing power and easy post-patent imitation squeeze margins.
A broad bucket of business-process outsourcing, banking, and information/consulting services; heterogeneity keeps this a moderate, unremarkable segment for a typical entrant.
Telecommunications transmission, casino/gaming systems and digital media hardware/software; licensing and infrastructure requirements favor established players.
Packaged foods, beverages and dairy products; grocery-retailer buyer power and easily copied recipes make this a tough category for new brands.
Insurance agency, benefits-administration and business/health consulting services; state licensing and broker relationships favor established incumbents.
Vehicle, aircraft and industrial machine parts manufacturing; certification requirements and large OEM buyers limit entry but reward qualified suppliers.
Specialty medical clinics (pain management, cosmetic surgery, ophthalmology) and related medical devices; licensure and device clearance create moderate barriers favoring capitalized entrants.
Streaming, broadcast and social/gaming entertainment platforms; strong network effects and content-distribution advantages make this winner-take-most, favoring whoever scales first.
Energy, fuel and oil-and-gas infrastructure/efficiency services; heavy capital and permitting requirements lock in incumbents who already hold the complementary assets.
Restaurants, cafes and food retail/bakery operations; notoriously low entry barriers and brutal competition make this one of the weakest long-run profit segments.
Banking, lending, insurance underwriting and employment-placement services; regulatory capital and licensing requirements favor incumbents over new entrants.
Hand tools, blades and power-tool accessories; retailer buyer power and manufacturing scale favor established tool brands over new entrants.
Cosmetics, hair-care products and salon services/equipment; low manufacturing barriers meet intense competition, so brand-building decides winners.
General and specialty retail store services spanning many product categories; e-commerce scale advantages and retailer concentration squeeze new entrants.

Pharmaceutical drug development across therapeutic areas; patent protection and the clinical-trial/regulatory gauntlet make this the clearest pioneer-advantage segment, held tightly by whoever gets there first.
Toys, games and sporting goods; easily copied products and retailer leverage favor brand owners with existing distribution over new entrants.
Alcoholic beverages, dairy and confectionery; alcohol licensing and the three-tier distribution system create real barriers, with brand incumbents holding the advantage.
HVAC and climate-control equipment plus installation/repair services; licensing requirements and dealer networks give moderate protection to established firms.
Telecom/data infrastructure equipment, electronic sensors and IT systems-integration services; a broad technology-services bucket without a single dominant structural advantage.
Skin-care, hair-care and personal-hygiene preparations; a near-pure CPG beauty category where formulations are trivially copied and big brands keep the margin.
Children's media and licensed-character merchandise spanning books, toys and video; licensing rights are the scarce asset, and incumbents who own them capture most of the value.
Water filtration and treatment equipment for residential and industrial use; certification standards and dealer networks offer modest protection without strong network effects.
Jewelry, watches and fine tableware/glassware; easily imitated designs mean brand reputation, not originality, sustains margins.
Industrial plastics, rubber, textiles and packaging materials; commodity-like inputs with capital-intensive manufacturing and strong buyer concentration among large OEMs.
Vitamins, dietary and sports-nutrition supplements; light-touch regulation makes entry easy, but that same ease invites flooding competition and copycats.
Mental-health counseling, wellness coaching and healthcare-consulting services; low capital needs and a fragmented market keep margins modest.
Orthopedic implants and surgical prosthetic devices; FDA clearance, surgeon-relationship capital and manufacturing precision make this hard to enter but rewarding for those who do.
Engineering, R&D and systems-design consulting for OEM, aerospace and government clients; expertise is the product, so advantage rests on reputation more than scale.
Construction management, real-estate development and waste/recycling-management services; licensing, bonding and track-record requirements favor established contractors.

A scattered mix of tobacco/smoking accessories, vehicle wheels/rims and equipment rental; tobacco licensing adds a barrier, but the grouping lacks a single coherent competitive structure, making it hard to rate as one business.
Live-event venues (theatre, casinos, zoos), religious/self-improvement media and educational seminars; low capital needs and high substitutability keep this fragmented.
Prepared foods, sauces and pizza/restaurant chains; a classically crowded, low-differentiation food category.
Apparel and home-textile basics; fast-fashion imitation and dominant retail buyers make this a difficult segment for new entrants to hold onto.
Industrial and agricultural machinery, parts, and equipment rental/financing; capital-intensive manufacturing and dealer/service networks favor incumbents.
Consumer mobile apps and cloud/social platforms; app-store gatekeepers and easily cloned features make this crowded, though network effects reward whoever scales fastest.
Live plants, seeds, fertilizers and lawn/pest-control services; plant-patent protection on novel cultivars gives a rare pocket of durable pioneer advantage within an otherwise low-barrier category.
Live music/entertainment, film production and video-game content; creative talent is cheap to start, but distribution and marketing muscle held by incumbents captures most value.
Broadcast media, live-event production and marketing/promotion/fundraising services; broadcast licensing adds a modest barrier, but overall this is a fragmented content business.
